chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'So do not swear by the places of the stars,' that: 'It was the people of ignorance who used to swear by it. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said:
So do not swear by the places of the stars
He (peace be upon him) said: 'The matter of the one who swears by it is great.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And the people of ignorance used to revere the Sacred Month (al-Muharram) and did not swear by it, nor by the month of Rajab, nor did they violate the sanctity of anyone who was traveling or returning during these two months, even if he had killed his father, nor for anything would they expel from the Sanctuary any beast, or sheep, or camel, or other than that.'
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): 'I swear by this city, and you are a dweller of this city.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'So it reached from their ignorance that they permitted the killing of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), while they revered the days of the month where they were swearing by it, so they would fulfill it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of swearing by the places of the stars and the city of Mecca in Shia exegesis?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the pre-Islamic Arabs' reverence for the sacred months and the Sanctuary was selective, as they honored these times for oaths and safe passage yet failed to protect the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his progeny) from assassination. This narrative underscores the theological principle that swearing by celestial bodies ('mawaqi' al-nujum') carries significant weight due to their perceived sanctity, while Allah's oath by Mecca in Surah Al-Balad serves to elevate the city's status above the idols and stars worshipped by the polytheists.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [56:75] So do not swear by the places of the stars said: ‘It was the people of ignorance who used to swear by it. Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic has Said [56:75] So do not swear by the places of the stars. It is a grievous matter the one who swears by it.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The (people of the) pre-Islamic period used to revere the Sanctuary and were not swearing by it, nor by the month of Rajab, nor were they violating to the one who was in these two, going or coming, even if his father had been killed, nor for anything would they expel from the Sanctuary any stray animal, or sheep, or camel, or other than that.
So Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Said to Hisazwj Prophetsaww [90:1] Indeed! I swear by this city [90:2] And you are a dweller of this city’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So it reached (to such an extent) from their ignorance, that they permitted the killing of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, whilst revering the days of the month where they were swearing by it, so they would fulfil it (the vows)’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas’adah ibn Sadaqah who has narrated the following: “

This is about the meaning of the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious. ‘I do not swear by the places of the stars.’ [56:75] Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘People of the community of ignorance swore by the places of stars and Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, said, “I do not swear by the places of stars.’”
He (the Imam) said that He called their swearing as such a grave thing.

He (the Imam) has said that people of the time of ignorance held the month of Muharram to be a great thing. They would not swear thereby as well as the month of Rajab and did not disturb in these months those going and coming around even if he may have killed one’s father. They would not expel from al- Haram (the Sacred area) an animal or sheep or camel and so on.

Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, said to His Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, ‘I do not swear by this town and you are living in this town.’ (90:2-3)

He (the Imam) said that their ignorance had climaxed to the level of making them to consider the killing of the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, as lawful. On the contrary they held days of the month with greatness whereby they swore and stood by such oaths.’”
